subject: Feed observed frontier reduction per resource into provider routing as a calibrated prior

body.text: Now that real carrier usage can retain input/cached/output/reasoning token dimensions and outcomes, connect execution economics to adaptive density without confusing resource use with money. Derive advisory, evidence-backed efficiency observations such as accepted-evidence-per-1k-input-tokens, solved-invariant/frontier-reduction-per-1k-total-tokens, wall-time-per-accepted-result, cache-reuse ratio, and retry waste for sufficiently comparable work classes. Keep provider/model/route coordinates nullable and pricing completely separate unless evidenced. These observations may become calibrated priors for the existing ProviderGraph/router or WorkGraph realization choice, never semantic authority and never a hard route gate by themselves. Record prediction vs realized outcome so the prior can be calibrated. Include Codex now; add Claude/local paths only where real comparable evidence exists. Required counterexample: a cheap/token-efficient route that produces weak evidence must not outrank a more expensive route merely because it used fewer tokens.
